**Finding submitted: deviation (IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data).**

What I found:
- **§7.0 Materials (p0082–p0086)** is the operative IP allocation. Type I Materials are Customer-owned, but the **default for undesignated Materials is Type II**, meaning IBM owns even work product created for us during the Service performance period.
- The **Type II licence back** is "irrevocable, nonexclusive, worldwide, paid-up ... within Customer's Enterprise only" — **no right to modify/create derivative works and no right to sublicense**, which fails the fallback position, not just the preferred one.
- **No Customer Data / Content ownership statement** anywhere; combined with §14.17 (only expressly granted licences), our retained rights in Content and Customer Components are unstated. There is no assignment of our IP/data to IBM and no joint ownership, so this is not walk-away.

Redline (validated ok:true, preferred level, 3 minimal ops):
1. p0082 — flip the default to Type I for Materials created during the Service performance period.
2. p0085 — make the Type II licence perpetual and add modify/derivative works and sublicensing rights for our business purposes (replacing the "Enterprise only" restriction).
3. New §7.e — confirm we retain all right, title and interest in Content, Customer Components and our data, with no assignment to IBM.

The broad licence we grant IBM in Type I Materials (p0084) is noted in the rationale but not flagged, since it is a licence rather than an assignment.
